scope: R194: the reduce-tile-count lever is capped at 1.089x by UB capacity
numeric_equivalence_note: retiling changes accumulation order so none of this is numerically equivalent; measurement only

failure_mechanism.scaling: the score tile in UB grows with Bc times Br times 2 bytes
failure_mechanism.why_512_fails: 131 KB for the score tile alone leaves too little for the Q/K/V sub-tiles, softmax temporaries and the output accumulator

reproducibility.verdict: both the measurement and the R193 linear model hold up

conclusion.lever_1_reduce_tiles: capped at 1.089x, about 0.6 s, far short of 1.50x
conclusion.lever_2_reduce_per_tile_cost: the only remaining route, potentially up to about 1.9x
conclusion.nature_of_remaining_work: not a configuration change but a kernel-implementation change inside MindIE's TIK kernel

final_fa_verdict.core_budget: ruled out, already the hardware limit (R188)
final_fa_verdict.softmax_op_reduction: ruled out, vector at most 21 percent (R190)
final_fa_verdict.pipeline_overlap: the only viable direction, requiring TIK kernel changes
final_fa_verdict.theoretical_payoff: removing the overhead entirely is 1.89x, enough for 1.50x (R193)

not_exhausted.idea: shrink Br while raising Bc (for example Br=64 with Bc=768), since the score tile size is the product Br*Bc and a different shape with the same product might still fit
not_exhausted.why_it_matters: this is the only parameter direction not yet tried
not_exhausted.note: it changes the q-block structure, so it deserves its own round

limits: only one shape tested (N=41792, padded to 43776); the UB ceiling may differ at other N
the exact remaining UB headroom was not itemised across the kernels other buffers
